title: Towards Disaggregated NDP Architectures for Large-scale Graph Analytics
problem: Large-scale graph analytics performance is fundamentally limited by memory subsystem capacity and performance constraints on traditional monolithic platforms. Existing approaches to scaling graph processing cannot overcome these memory bottlenecks.
motivation: Memory system constraints are critical performance limiters for large-scale graph processing and require architectural innovations to address.
method: The paper proposes disaggregated architectures with near-data processing (NDP) capabilities to overcome memory limitations. It performs experimental analysis of trade-offs across different graph types and analytics kernels to identify systems-level mechanisms needed for future frameworks to effectively leverage disaggregated NDP.
key_novelty: Using disaggregated near-data processing architectures to overcome memory system bottlenecks in graph analytics.
contributions: Analysis of limitations in existing graph processing scaling approaches
Proposal of disaggregated NDP solutions to address memory bottlenecks
Identification of required systems-level mechanisms for future graph frameworks
Experimental trade-off analysis for different graph types and analytics kernels

metrics.other: performance improvements not quantified in abstract

limitations: Specific quantitative performance improvements, implementation details, and concrete comparisons with state-of-the-art systems not discussed.
